prerequisites: Fluid Mechanics from 2nd year, second semester
Physics I and II, Mathematics I and II from first year
Advanced Mathematics and Thermal Engineering from first semester of second year

learning_outcomes.text: Students must be able to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.

Students must have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that starts from the basis of general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
Students must have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students must know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students must be able to transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Ability to work, lead, and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to transmit information orally and in writing, adapted to the audience.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability to understand and apply the basic principles of general, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and its application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels and fluid systems.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts of general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.
Basic knowledge of the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and software applications in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to fluid machines. Generalities and classification.
Energy balance in turbomachinery. Basic magnitudes, efficiencies. Introduction to pumping and turbining installations.

Ideal theory of hydraulic turbomachinery. Velocity diagram, conservation equations of mass, momentum, angular momentum and energy. Euler equation. Bernoulli equation in relative motion. Degree of reaction. Efficiencies.
Physical similarity in turbomachinery: Introduction to dimensional analysis, dimensionless parameters and similarity relations.
Characteristic diagrams and pump testing. Specific speed and diameter. Influence of roughness and viscosity.

Theory of centrifugal turbomachinery: Theory of centrifugal pumps. Unidimensional theory, influence of outlet blade angle, degree of reaction. Real characteristic curves, losses and efficiencies. Bidimensional theory: corrections.

Theory of axial turbomachinery. Ideal bidimensional theory. Airfoil lift, fixed cascade of airfoils, bidimensional motion in the rotor (moving cascade). Stator-rotor assembly. Degree of reaction. Real curves.
Introduction to hydraulic turbines. Generalities. Classification. Operation of a centripetal turbine in variable regime, characteristic curves.
Description of different types of turbines: Francis turbines, propeller and Kaplan turbines, Pelton turbines: parts, components, operating curves and regulation.
Cavitation in turbomachinery. Cavitation in pumps, cavitation tests. Specific cavitation speed. Thoma's parameter. Cavitation in turbines.
Sizing and calculation of pumping and turbining installations. Stability and start-up of pumps. Pump selection. Calculation of installations.
Laboratory practices with 5 different hydraulic machines: centrifugal pump, pumps in series/parallel, axial turbine, Francis turbine and Pelton turbine.
teaching_methods: Exposition of theory and general examples

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theoretical concepts of the subject (Written test)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (Correction of submitted reports)
Laboratory/field practices/use of ICT tools (Correction of laboratory practice reports)

assessment_rules: The grading system will be governed by RD 1125/2003. A minimum grade must be obtained in the written test (70% weight) for other components to be taken into account and to pass the subject. The student must have attended all laboratory practice sessions to be eligible to take the written test. Resit arrangements are not explicitly mentioned.
